name: Trojan War
content:
The Trojan War was a legendary conflict in Greek mythology, waged by the
Achaeans (Greeks) against the city of Troy after Paris of Troy took Helen from
her husband Menelaus, king of Sparta. The war is the central subject of
Homer's Iliad, and its aftermath is covered in the Odyssey and other works of
the Epic Cycle (like the Aeneid, which follows the Trojan survivor Aeneas).
Traditionally dated to the 12th or 13th century BC, the ten-year siege ended
when the Greeks tricked the Trojans with the Trojan Horse, a hollow wooden
horse filled with soldiers, built by Epeius and gifted as a "peace offering."
Key figures include Achilles and Hector (whose duel is the climax of the
Iliad), Agamemnon (leader of the Greek forces), Odysseus (who devised the
horse), Priam (king of Troy), and Paris (whose "Judgment of Paris" — choosing
Aphrodite as fairest of the goddesses in exchange for Helen's love — set the
war in motion). The gods themselves take sides throughout: Hera, Athena, and
Poseidon back the Greeks, while Aphrodite, Apollo, and Ares favor the
Trojans. Archaeological excavations at Hisarlik in modern Turkey, begun by
Heinrich Schliemann in the 1870s, uncovered multiple destruction layers,
lending some historical plausibility to a real Bronze Age conflict behind the
myth, even though the gods, prophecies, and the horse itself are not
considered literal history.

Key figures:
Achilles: the greatest Greek warrior, famed for his near invincibility except for his heel.
Hector: the greatest Trojan warrior and eldest son of King Priam.
Agamemnon: the king of Mycenae and commander of the combined Greek forces.
Paris: the Trojan prince whose abduction of Helen triggered the war.
Helen: the wife of Menelaus whose abduction by Paris sparked the conflict.
Trojan Horse: the hollow wooden horse used by the Greeks to smuggle soldiers into Troy.

questions.question: According to legend, whose abduction by Paris triggered the Trojan War?
questions.answer: Helen of Sparta

questions.question: Which epic poem, attributed to Homer, tells the story of the Trojan War itself?
questions.answer: The Iliad

questions.question: Who built the Trojan Horse?
questions.answer: Epeius

questions.question: Which Greek hero killed Hector, the greatest Trojan warrior?
questions.answer: Achilles

questions.question: Who was the king of Troy during the war?
questions.answer: Priam

questions.question: Which goddess did Paris choose as "fairest" in the Judgment of Paris, setting the war in motion?
questions.answer: Aphrodite

questions.question: Who commanded the combined Greek forces at Troy?
questions.answer: Agamemnon

questions.question: According to tradition, roughly how long did the siege of Troy last?
questions.answer: Ten years

questions.question: Which archaeologist excavated the site at Hisarlik believed to be Troy?
questions.answer: Heinrich Schliemann

questions.question: Which Trojan survivor's journey to found a new home in Italy is told in Virgil's Aeneid?
questions.answer: Aeneas

questions.question: What triggered the Trojan War?
questions.answer: Paris of Troy took Helen, wife of King Menelaus of Sparta, back to Troy — provoking a Greek expedition to retrieve her.

questions.question: What is the Trojan Horse?
questions.answer: A large hollow wooden horse the Greeks built and left outside Troy's gates as a fake "peace offering," secretly filled with soldiers who opened the city gates at night.

questions.question: Who were Achilles and Hector?
questions.answer: The greatest warriors of the Greek and Trojan sides respectively; their duel, ending in Hector's death, is the climax of the Iliad.

questions.question: What is the "Judgment of Paris"?
questions.answer: A mythic contest where Paris chose Aphrodite as the fairest goddess over Hera and Athena, in exchange for the love of the world's most beautiful woman — Helen.

questions.question: What work covers the Trojan War itself, and what work covers its aftermath for Odysseus?
questions.answer: The Iliad covers the war (specifically a few weeks near its end); the Odyssey covers Odysseus's ten-year journey home afterward.

questions.question: Which side did the gods Hera, Athena, and Poseidon support?
questions.answer: The Greeks (Achaeans).

questions.question: Which side did the gods Aphrodite, Apollo, and Ares support?
questions.answer: The Trojans.

questions.question: What happened to Aeneas after the fall of Troy?
questions.answer: He escaped the burning city and, per Virgil's Aeneid, eventually journeyed to Italy, where his descendants were said to found Rome.

questions.question: Is there archaeological evidence for a real Trojan War?
questions.answer: Excavations at Hisarlik in Turkey (started by Heinrich Schliemann) found multiple destruction layers from the Bronze Age, suggesting a real conflict may lie behind the myth — though the gods and the horse are not treated as literal history.

questions.question: Who was Menelaus?
questions.answer: King of Sparta and Helen's husband; his brother Agamemnon led the Greek expedition to Troy to bring her back.
